name: Crying Wojak Vs Chad
core: A hysterical, crying side yelling an argument while a calm, confident Chad replies coolly.
avoid: Not for two equally reasonable positions.

name: Why Not Zoidberg
core: Suggesting an obviously bad, desperate option with "Need X? Why not Zoidberg?".

name: Jackie Chan Confused
core: Utter bafflement at something that makes no logical sense.
avoid: Not for things that are clear and sensible.

name: Bad Joke Eel
core: Telling a terrible pun or anti-joke, with the setup on top and the groan-worthy punchline below.
avoid: Not for genuinely clever jokes or serious points.

name: Pie Chart
core: A pie chart where one thing takes up almost everything and the other is a sliver, showing a lopsided split.

name: Naruto Handshake
core: Two rival groups shaking hands, showing what unlikely sides agree on.
avoid: Not for one-sided situations with no common ground.

name: Bear Grylls
core: Survival-expert advice that solves a problem in the most extreme or disgusting way possible.

name: Get This Man A Shield
core: Praising someone brave enough to say a bold, unpopular truth: get this man a shield.
avoid: Not for cowardly or uncontroversial statements.

name: Bonjour Polar Bear
core: A polar bear popping out of a snow hole to cheerfully say "bonjour", for awkwardly showing up or popping in unexpectedly.
avoid: Not for serious or tense moments.

name: Say What Again
core: Daring someone to repeat something annoying one more time: "say X again, I dare you".
avoid: Not for friendly or calm conversations.

name: Meg You Think You're Better Than Me
core: Meg indignantly accusing someone of thinking they're better than her, answered by the family in top hats smugly confirming it.
aliases: meg family guy better than me
you think you're better than me

name: Patrick Says
core: Patrick confidently raising a finger to share a dumb or naively literal piece of wisdom.

name: Laughing Kid
core: A kid laughing hysterically at someone else's misfortune or a ridiculous situation.
avoid: Not for sympathetic or sad moments.

name: Maybe I Am A Monster
core: Vision accepting that his unpopular habit or opinion makes him a monster: "Maybe I am a ___".

name: Soldier Jump Attack
core: One soldier leaping through the air to ambush another who is completely unaware, for a sudden surprise attack.
avoid: Not for situations where the target sees it coming.

name: Snape
core: Snape recoiling in pained shock, for reacting to something unbearable or outrageous.
avoid: Not for happy or calm reactions.

name: No I Don't Think I Will
core: Old Captain America calmly and smugly refusing a request or suggestion.
aliases: no i don't think i will

name: Venn Diagram
core: Two overlapping circles showing two groups and the surprising thing they have in common.
avoid: Not for things with nothing in common.

name: The Count
core: The Count gleefully counting up something that keeps piling up, ah ah ah.
avoid: Not for things that can't be counted or aren't repeating.

name: Squidward Talking To SpongeBob
core: Squidward whispering advice to SpongeBob, then pointing him off somewhere, for telling someone exactly what to do or where to go.

name: Robert Downey Jr's Comments
core: Robert Downey Jr pointing at himself in mock surprise, as if to say "who, me?" about something he clearly did.
aliases: robert downey jr pointing at himself
avoid: Not for situations where the person is truly innocent.

name: Excited Cat
core: A kitten with a wide-open mouth, overjoyed and excited about something.

name: Smiling Jesus
core: A beaming, serene Jesus cheerfully approving of or forgiving something, often with a wholesome or ironic twist.
avoid: Not for mocking anyone's faith or real tragedies.

name: Fastest Things On Earth
core: A speed ranking of cheetah, airplane and light, topped by something everyday that happens absurdly fast.
avoid: Not for slow things, unless the joke is ironic.

name: No Fear One Fear
core: A tough guy with a NO FEAR shirt meets one thing and his shirt changes to ONE FEAR.
avoid: Not for things that inspire no fear at all.

name: SpongeBob Hype Stand
core: SpongeBob sets up a stand selling something and an enormous crowd swarms to get it.

name: Phteven
core: An overbitten dog with a lisp; used to mispronounce a word or make a goofy, awkward statement.

name: Jim Peeking Through Blinds
core: Jim grinning through office blinds; used when you secretly watch someone's plan or mistake play out.

name: SpongeBob Office Fire
core: Many SpongeBobs panicking in a burning office; used for total chaos and panic.

name: Satisfied Seal vs Awkward Seal
core: A smug seal, then the awkward seal; used when brief satisfaction turns into an uncomfortable realisation.

name: Challenge Accepted
core: The smug rage-comic face; used when you take on a dare or a ridiculous self-imposed challenge.

name: The What
core: A retro ad woman whose zoomed face reads 'The WHAT'; used to react to something absurd you just heard.

name: How Dare You
core: Greta Thunberg glaring mid-speech; used for mock outrage at someone's offence.
avoid: Genuinely serious climate or political attacks.

name: Chocolate SpongeBob
core: SpongeBob offers something and the man screams it back; used when someone reacts to a thing with desperate, overblown hunger.

name: Please Sir, May I Have Some More
core: Oliver Twist holding out his bowl; used to beg for more of something, often something bad.

name: Groundhog Day
core: Bill Murray reporting in Groundhog Day; used when the same thing happens again and again.

name: Evil Baby
core: A baby glaring furiously; used for petty rage or plotting revenge.

name: Pinky And The Brain
core: Pinky and the Brain; used as 'Are you pondering what I'm pondering?' with an absurd answer or plan.
aliases: are you pondering what im pondering

name: If I Had One
core: Mr. Crocker shows where he'd put something, then sobs that he doesn't have one; used for lacking something you'd want.
slots: this is where I'd put my...
aliases: this is where id put my

name: Drooling Shape Puzzle
core: A drooling idiot fails a baby shape-sorting toy; used to mock someone failing at something trivially easy.

name: Corporate Needs You To Find The Differences
core: Pam says two pictures are the same; used when two things claimed to be different are identical.

name: Bonk
core: A dog bonks another with a bat; used to swiftly punish someone for a bad take.

name: Are We The Baddies?
core: A soldier in a skull-cap realises his side might be the villains; used when you notice you're the bad guy.

name: Successful Black Man
core: An advice-animal guy in a suit; the top line leads you to expect a stereotype and the bottom line turns into a successful, responsible twist.
avoid: Racial jokes; the twist must stay wholesome.

name: Silence, X, A Y Is Talking
core: A masked king hushes someone; used to silence a lesser group when a 'superior' one speaks.
aliases: silence x a y is talking

name: Interrupting Kanye
core: Kanye grabs the mic from Taylor Swift; used when something barges in and steals the spotlight.

name: Oops! All Berries
core: A Cap'n Crunch box reading 'Oops! All...'; used when something is nothing but one (usually bad) thing.
slots: picture or thing in the bowl

name: Hangover Math
core: Alan from The Hangover doing mental math; used for overthinking a simple calculation.

name: Futuristic Utopia
core: A shining future city; used as 'if X had happened, we'd be here by now'.

name: It's More Likely Than You Think
core: A PC-check ad: 'X? In my Y? It's more likely than you think'; used to warn about a surprising hidden problem.

name: In Terms Of Money, We Have No Money
core: Gru telling the minions there's none of something; used as 'In terms of X, we have no X'.
slots: in terms of X, we have no X

name: You Have No Power Here
core: Gandalf telling Saruman/Théoden 'you have no power here'; used to dismiss someone's authority in a place.

name: We're The Millers
core: Four shocked faces from We're the Millers; used when a group reacts in shock to something absurd.

name: Adios
core: A man walks into a glowing portal with 'Adiós'; used for leaving something behind for good.

name: Vanya And Five
core: Two siblings in passing cars spot each other; used when two people catch each other somewhere they shouldn't be.

name: Bill Murray Golf
core: Bill Murray tossing his club and waving; used for cheerfully not caring or giving up.

name: Happy Picard
core: Picard pumping his fists in delight, used to celebrate a small, satisfying victory.
avoid: Not for disappointment or facepalm moments; that's Picard Facepalm.

name: Emperor Palpatine
core: Palpatine grinning wickedly, used to egg on a bad idea or gloat as a scheme comes together.

name: Happy Squirrel
core: A squirrel throwing its arms up in joy, used to celebrate good news or praise the heavens.
avoid: Not for sad or annoyed reactions.

name: Ronald McDonald on the Phone
core: Ronald McDonald taking a phone call, used for an absurd or ominous call he answers or makes.
